Eritrean Migrant Released from Prison, Avoided Deportation, Raped Woman Soon After 

  • CURRENT

Eritrean Migrant Released from Prison, Avoided Deportation, Raped Woman Soon After 

Eritrean illegal migrant Radiet Meles
X
An Eritrean illegal migrant who remained in Britain after an attempted-rape conviction and an apparent expectation of deportation has now been convicted of raping another woman in Wales. Radiet Meles, 35, entered the UK illegally in 2015, was jailed for five years in 2019, but was never removed and later returned to Newport, where he raped another woman almost immediately.
  • Joakim Scheffer
  • — 14.09.2026

Instaread

An Eritrean illegal migrant who remained in Britain despite being convicted of attempted rape and ordered to leave the country has now been found guilty of raping another woman in Wales, United Kingdom.

Radiet Meles, 35, was unanimously convicted of rape and assault by beating following a five-day trial at Cardiff Crown Court. The offences concerned an attack on a woman in Newport, South Wales, in March 2026. Meles denied both charges.

The Eritrean migrant, a former soldier, entered Britain illegally in 2015. During an earlier court case, he said through a Tigrinya interpreter that he had travelled from France in a lorry through the Channel Tunnel. He was held in Dover for two days before going to Cardiff and later settling in Newport, where he worked at a food-packaging factory, Amazon, and a car wash.

His first serious sexual offence took place on 13 August 2018. Meles was accused of raping a heavily intoxicated woman at a house party in Newport. Prosecutors said the victim remembered virtually nothing of what happened there and next recalled waking in an ambulance.

Meles denied sexual contact. At his trial in February 2019, a jury acquitted him of rape but convicted him of attempted rape. He was sentenced to five years in prison.

Judge Christopher Vosper told Meles that he had recognized the woman was effectively unconscious and intended to take advantage of her. More significantly for what followed, Vosper also warned him that after his release he was likely to be held in an immigration detention centre and that, given his offence and sentence, the Home Secretary was ‘likely to make a deportation order’ against him.

But Meles was never deported. After leaving prison, he remained in Britain and returned to Newport. No official explanation has emerged publicly for why he was not removed. Media and social-media reporting do not establish whether a deportation order was formally made, whether Meles mounted an asylum or human-rights challenge, whether another legal or administrative obstacle prevented his removal, or whether he simply evaded expulsion.

In March 2026, Meles was arrested after another woman was assaulted, once again in Newport. He was subsequently charged with rape and assault by beating and has now been convicted of both offences.

Recorder Andrew Hammond warned Meles that he faces a ‘lengthy custodial’ sentence. He is due to be sentenced at Cardiff Crown Court on 20 November.
